title: Chapter 69 — The Funeral
paragraphs: "Haul in the chains! Let the carcass go astern!"

The vast tackles have now done their duty. The peeled white body of the beheaded whale gleams like a marble tomb; though changed in color, it has not visibly lost anything in bulk. It is still colossal. Slowly it floats farther and farther away, the water around it torn and splashed by the insatiable sharks, and the air above harassed by rapacious flights of screaming birds, whose beaks are like so many insulting daggers in the whale. The vast white headless phantom floats farther and farther from the ship, and with every rod that it floats, what seem square roods of sharks and cubic roods of birds swell the murderous din. For hours and hours that hideous sight can be seen from the almost motionless ship. Beneath the unclouded, mild blue sky, upon the fair face of the pleasant sea, carried along by the joyous breezes, that great mass of death floats on and on, till it is lost in infinite perspectives.

What a doleful and mocking funeral this is! The sea-vultures all in pious mourning, the air-sharks all correctly dressed in black or speckled. Few of them, I suspect, would have lifted a finger for the whale in life, had he happened to need it; but at the banquet of his funeral they pounce with the greatest piety. Oh, the horrible vultureism of the earth, from which not even the mightiest whale is exempt!

Nor is this the end. Desecrated as the body is, a vengeful ghost survives and hovers over it to frighten. Sighted from afar by some timid warship or blundering discovery-vessel — when the distance hides the swarming birds but still shows the white mass floating in the sun, and the white spray heaving high against it — straightaway the whale's harmless corpse is set down in the log with trembling fingers: "Shoals, rocks, and breakers hereabouts: beware!" And for years afterward, perhaps, ships avoid the place, leaping over it as silly sheep leap over empty air, because their leader originally leaped there when a stick was held up. There's your law of precedents; there's your usefulness of traditions; there's the story of your stubborn survival of old beliefs never grounded on the earth, and now not even hovering in the air! There's orthodoxy!
So while the great whale's living body may have been a real terror to his enemies, once he is dead his ghost becomes a powerless panic to a whole world.
Do you believe in ghosts, my friend? There are other ghosts besides the Cock-Lane one (the famous London ghost hoax of 1762), and men far deeper than Doctor Johnson believe in them.
